open_points.subject: A13 owner-session cookie
open_points.text: "carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine, and only to Registry's own origin" does not define the cookie's host/domain, path, SameSite policy, browser lifetime, or whether Secure is required on locally reached HTTP
open_points.question: What exact cookie attributes and transport rule carry an owner session, including whether a locally reached interface may use the cookie over HTTP?
options: Host-only, Path=/, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, always Secure
Host-only and HttpOnly, Secure only when the request used HTTPS, with a stated SameSite and lifetime
Another explicit cookie policy
open_points.default_guess: Use a host-only, Path=/, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie; require Secure whenever Registry is served over HTTPS and make its browser lifetime no longer than the server session.

open_points.subject: A13 pending confirmation
open_points.text: "one-time" and "is used up by the first submission that carries it" do not say that checking and consuming the pending confirmation is one atomic, serialised transition
open_points.question: When two submissions concurrently carry the same valid confirmation value, must exactly one be allowed past confirmation checking, and when is the value atomically consumed?
options: Atomically consume it before either action proceeds, so exactly one submission can continue
Serialise the complete confirmed actions and let the first one consume it
Permit both submissions that passed a concurrent check
open_points.default_guess: Atomically compare and consume the pending value before the action proceeds, allowing exactly one submission to continue.

open_points.subject: A13 idle lifetime
open_points.text: "the instant of its last request" and "An owner request ... restarts the 30 minutes" do not define how concurrent requests update that instant or prevent a later-finishing older request from moving it backwards
open_points.question: Is last_request the maximum arrival instant of all requests that passed session validation, and must its update be atomic?
options: Store the maximum qualifying request-arrival instant atomically
Use transaction or completion order
Serialise all requests in an owner session
open_points.default_guess: Atomically retain the maximum arrival instant of requests that pass session validation.

open_points.subject: A15 dated audit erasure
open_points.text: "The date of an erasure is a date not later than today, the current date in UTC" does not say at which instant during a request today is determined
open_points.question: If an erasure request crosses UTC midnight, is its date validated against the date when the request arrives, when the value check runs, or when the transaction commits?
options: Request-arrival date
Value-check date
Transaction-commit date
open_points.default_guess: Use the UTC date at the value check performed inside the erasure transaction.

open_points.subject: A16 mapping scope
open_points.text: Rule 1 says the mapping shows "every malformed record and every id that conflicts with one production holds", while rule 3 says records only of unpicked projects "are neither checked, shown as conflicts nor imported"
open_points.question: Does the mapping report and validate malformed records and conflicting ids throughout the file, or only within the selected projects and the records they bring?
options: Only selected projects and their brought records
The whole file, although only selected projects are imported
Show whole-file problems but refuse only for problems in selected records
open_points.default_guess: Check, show, and use for refusal only the selected projects and their brought records.

open_points.subject: A16 duplicate project ids
open_points.text: "As the owner picks projects" is not defined for a file in which "an id occurs twice among the file's records of one kind"
open_points.question: How is a project selected when two project records have the same id, and is that duplicate checked before selection or only after one of those records is considered picked?
options: Duplicate project ids make the file's project selection malformed before any pick can identify one
Selecting the duplicated id brings both records and refuses the import
The interface assigns file-record identities distinct from project ids for selection
open_points.default_guess: Treat duplicate project ids as a mapping error before they can be selected.

open_points.subject: A16 malformed imported values
open_points.text: The exhaustive-looking rule "A brought-in record is malformed when" mentions statuses and artifact types but does not say what happens when an imported object's kind or another imported closed-vocabulary value is outside its declared vocabulary
open_points.question: Which State 1 and State 6 field constraints, beyond the cases enumerated in A16 rule 4, are applied to brought-in records?
options: Every ordinary record constraint and closed vocabulary applies to imported records
Only the cases explicitly enumerated in A16 rule 4 apply
State 6 will declare a separate complete import-validation set
open_points.default_guess: Apply every ordinary structural, required-value, and closed-vocabulary constraint, plus A16's import-specific history checks.

open_points.subject: A16 refused confirmation state
open_points.text: Rule 2 says "A refused confirmation keeps [the uploaded file]", while rule 9 says "nothing of a refused attempt remains"
open_points.question: After a refused import confirmation, which session state remains: the uploaded file, mapping inputs or picks, and any pending confirmation?
options: Keep only the uploaded file; consume the confirmation and recompute or reshow the mapping
Remove all upload and mapping state
Keep the file and the complete mapping submission
open_points.default_guess: Keep the uploaded file, consume the confirmation as A13 requires, store no attempted import or mapping submission, and require the step to be shown again.

open_points.subject: A16 file digest
open_points.text: "The mapping names the file by its digest" and the confirmation and migration closure are bound to that digest, but no digest algorithm or definition of the digested bytes is given
open_points.question: Which collision-resistant algorithm is used, and is the digest over the exact uploaded bytes or over a parsed or canonicalised representation?
options: A specified cryptographic digest over the exact uploaded bytes
A specified cryptographic digest over a canonicalised import representation
A release-dependent digest declared in State 6
open_points.default_guess: Use SHA-256 over the exact uploaded bytes and record the algorithm with the digest if algorithms may ever change.

open_points.subject: A17 store and backup locations
open_points.text: The checks require writable store and backup locations but do not say whether they may be the same path, overlap, contain one another, or resolve through symbolic links
open_points.question: What path relationships and filesystem object types are valid for the store and backup location, and which unsafe configurations must stop startup?
options: Require distinct resolved locations, a regular store file and a dedicated backup directory, with stated symlink handling
Allow the store inside the backup directory while reserving non-colliding names
Allow any writable paths and rely on filename conventions
open_points.default_guess: Require a regular store file and a distinct dedicated backup directory after path resolution, and reject ambiguous or unsafe symlink relationships.

open_points.subject: A18 failed daily run
open_points.text: A run missed while stopped is made at the next start "if no backup was made that UTC day", but there is "at most one run per UTC day" and a failed run "is tried again at the next run"
open_points.question: Does a failed attempt count as that day's one run, and may a later restart on the same UTC day retry it?
options: A failed attempt consumes the daily run; retry on the next day's run
A failed attempt does not count as a made backup and may retry later the same day
Permit one successful daily backup but any number of failed attempts
open_points.default_guess: Permit at most one scheduled attempt per UTC day and retry a failure at the next scheduled or explicitly required run, not at another ordinary restart that day.

open_points.subject: A18 backup retention after failure
open_points.text: Rule 5 deletes expired backups "whether the new backup succeeded or not", but rule 7 says "a failed run lengthens" the time for an erasure to reach backups
open_points.question: Does failure of creating or checking the new backup delay deletion of backups older than 30 days, or does only a deletion failure delay it?
options: Deletion still runs after backup failure; only deletion failure extends retention
Any failure in the run postpones retention deletion
Delete expired backups only after a new checked backup exists
open_points.default_guess: Run retention deletion independently; only a deletion failure extends how long an erased value remains in backups.

open_points.subject: A18 backup cryptography
open_points.text: "Each backup is encrypted with the backup key" and records "a digest of the key", but the encryption construction, nonce handling, authentication of ciphertext and metadata, key-digest algorithm, and format version are not declared
open_points.question: What exact authenticated-encryption and backup-envelope format must every implementation use, and which metadata is authenticated?
options: Specify a versioned authenticated-encryption envelope with unique nonces and authenticate all metadata
Leave the algorithm release-specific but require the release to declare and test it
Permit encryption without authenticated metadata
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned AEAD envelope with a fresh random nonce per backup, authenticate all cleartext metadata, and specify a cryptographic key identifier digest.

open_points.subject: A18 backup verification
open_points.text: Registry checks "that the store's own integrity check passes" without defining that check or the corruption classes it must detect
open_points.question: What exact store-level verification constitutes a passed checked backup, beyond opening it, matching its version and checking the audit sequence?
options: Declare backend-specific full structural integrity checks and required semantic invariants
Only require the storage engine's standard integrity-check operation
Opening the store successfully is sufficient
open_points.default_guess: Require the storage engine's full integrity check plus explicit checks of schema/version, referential constraints and the stated audit counter.

open_points.subject: A18 temporary-file cleanup
open_points.text: At every run Registry first removes temporary files, and "a removal that fails is reported and tried again at the next run", but the text does not say whether that run then continues with backup creation and retention deletion
open_points.question: If cleanup of a stale encrypted or decrypted temporary file fails, does the current run abort, continue its safe parts, or create new temporary files alongside it?
options: Abort backup creation but still attempt safe retention deletion
Abort the entire run
Continue if new unique temporary names cannot collide
open_points.default_guess: Abort new backup creation after cleanup failure, report it, and still attempt deletion of independently identifiable expired kept backups.

open_points.subject: A01 create replay equality
open_points.text: "the facts it supplies equal that record's current facts" and "Facts are compared as A02 reads them" define blank strings but do not define equality for structured object characteristics or other non-scalar values
open_points.question: What is semantic equality for every create input, especially structured characteristics: exact encoded representation, ordered structure, or canonical value equality?
options: Canonical typed-value equality, with map order irrelevant and list order as declared by the schema
Exact submitted representation equality
State 6 declares equality separately for every field
open_points.default_guess: Compare parsed typed values canonically, treating object/map key order as irrelevant and preserving list order only where the field's model makes it meaningful.

open_points.subject: A01 replay after artifact-type removal
open_points.text: R0-88 says a publish retry that is still allowed because "the project [is] still in the session's set and not archived" returns its pointer, while A01 requires the current type check again and test 11 says a retry after type removal is refused
open_points.question: Does removal of an artifact type invalidate a replay of a publish that already succeeded, or does the request id still return the existing pointer?
options: Return the existing pointer when access and project lifecycle checks still pass
Refuse the replay because the type is no longer declared
Treat replay lookup before current vocabulary validation
open_points.default_guess: Return the existing pointer after current authorization and project-lifecycle checks; type removal should prevent new publication, not retrieval of the result of an already accepted request.

open_points.subject: A04 check ordering within a stage
open_points.text: The text orders stages (1) through (6), but says only that "each check an operation states belongs to the stage of its kind" and gives no order among multiple failing checks in the same stage
open_points.question: When several checks in one stage fail, which failure is returned—for example two invalid values, or an archived project together with an ineligible customer or id conflict?
options: Declare a total per-operation order inside every stage
Define one indistinguishable refusal for all failures within a stage
Allow any same-stage failure to win
open_points.default_guess: Declare a deterministic per-operation order, while keeping authorization-hiding failures indistinguishable where required.

open_points.subject: A04 existence of related records
open_points.text: Stage (3) checks "that the record named exists", while stage (6) includes "a customer's eligibility"; a project correction may name both its project and a new customer, and State 0 says an unknown customer is refused
open_points.question: At which stage is existence of a newly named customer checked, and does an unknown customer win before value and revision failures or only with the other customer-eligibility checks at stage 6?
options: Check every referenced record's existence at stage 3
At stage 3 check only the primary target; check a related customer's existence and eligibility together at stage 6
Declare the placement separately per operation
open_points.default_guess: Check the primary target at stage 3 and check the newly referenced customer's existence, erased/restricted/ended state together at stage 6.

open_points.subject: MigrationClosure persistence after restore
open_points.text: M10 still says "Durable, at most one per instance", while R0-89 now permits the same restored production installation to lose the closure and perform the import again
open_points.question: Is the at-most-one invariant scoped to an installation or instance across disaster recovery, or only to one store history?
options: At most one closure and accepted import per store history
At most one accepted import for the installation even if the closure was lost
A restore creates a formally new Registry instance
open_points.default_guess: Scope the invariant to one store history; a pre-import backup restore starts a new history in which one import may be accepted.
